threads.thread_goal: Lock capsule concept, theme, and target customer before detailed design.

messages.text:
Kicking off the capsule concept thread for Launch Capsule Collection With Integrated Visual Identity.
I dropped a first draft of the Capsule Concept and Moodboard in A1, mapped loosely to T1.
Working title: 'Urban Drift' – lightweight layers for transitional weather, with subtle tech details.
Initial thoughts:
- Target: late 20s to mid 30s, city-based, already familiar with our brand
- Use: commute, casual office, weekend
- Price: slightly above our core line, but below collab pricing
Before we go deeper into sketches, I would like to confirm if we are leaning more street-led or minimal-tailored, and how bold we can go on color vs our current brand palette.
Can you all react with your preference and any must-have constraints from your side?

Thanks for starting this.
Looking at A1, I see a nice balance between utility and softer textures.
My instinct is to keep silhouettes clean and let fabric and small construction details carry the story, so more minimal-tailored with a few street cues.
On color, I would stay close to our existing neutrals and add 1–2 accent tones that we can source easily from the current supplier list.
For the target, I agree with city-based, but I would also include people who work hybrid and need pieces that move from home to office to evening.
Happy to adjust once we hear from the visual side.

I went through A1 as well.
From a construction and sizing standpoint, a minimal-tailored base will be easier to keep consistent across sizes, especially if we want to move fast on specs later.
If we keep the tech details subtle (pockets, fastenings, panel lines), we can still nod to streetwear without adding complex pattern pieces.
On price, slightly above core line sounds realistic as long as we do not introduce exotic fabrics that are not already in our supplier list.
I would suggest we define early which garments are outer layers vs base layers so we can plan comfort and fit checks in T10 later.

From the visual identity side, the mood in A1 already leans into calm, structured, and slightly techy.
If we go minimal-tailored with subtle street details, I can keep the capsule identity in line with our main brand while adding a sharper edge in typography and layout later in A3 and T5.
For color, I would recommend one signature accent that can show up both in garments and in graphics, plus a secondary accent that we use mostly in digital.
That will help us keep e-commerce and social assets cohesive without overwhelming the garments.

I like the 'Urban Drift' direction.
Looking at A1, I see some images that feel more sporty.
Do we want to keep any of that, or should we remove those from the moodboard so it is clearer for later tasks like T7 and T9?
Also, for the target customer, are we including students or focusing only on people already in full-time work?

Good catch on the sporty references.
I added those mainly for fabric and movement cues.
I can trim A1 so the core story is clearer and move the sportier shots into a secondary section just for construction inspiration.
On the target, I would keep the primary focus on early-career professionals and freelancers in cities.
Students can still buy, but I would not design specifically for campus use.
If no one objects, I will update the target description in T1 accordingly.

Aligning with that target sounds good to me.
For the narrative, I would frame it around moving through different zones in the city in one day: commute, desk, evening.
That will help us later when we map SKUs and looks.
On price, I suggest we define a band like: tops slightly above core, outerwear closer to our premium line, so we do not end up with random gaps.
We can refine once we see fabric choices in T11.

Agree on the day-in-the-city narrative.
From a manufacturing view, that also gives us a clear split between lighter pieces and more structured ones.
For price bands, I will draft a quick internal note based on our usual cost ranges so we do not overbuild any single SKU.
We should also note in T1 that we are not introducing new fabric bases, only new combinations and finishes from the existing supplier list, to reduce risk on lead times.

For the story, I can echo that day-in-the-city arc in the visual identity and later in the Internal Capsule Overview Deck A8.
We can structure the narrative as three moments and show how each look fits into them.
On price positioning, as long as we stay slightly elevated but not luxury, I can keep the graphic language refined but still approachable.
I will wait for the final wording in T1 before I start sketching identity routes in T5.

If we are not adding new fabric bases, should we already list which ones we want to highlight in A1 or in a separate note?
I am asking because it might influence how we shoot textures later for e-commerce guidelines in A6 and T7.
Also, for the target age range, are we locking it at late 20s to mid 30s, or do we want to keep it a bit wider?

On fabrics, I can add a short list of hero bases to A1 and then expand it properly when we build the SKU and Colorway Matrix A2 under T11.
That should give you enough direction for texture and lighting later.
For age, I would phrase it as: style-conscious city dwellers roughly 25–38, but design for attitude and use case more than strict age.
If everyone is comfortable with that, we can consider the target profile and price band defined for T1.

The age and attitude framing works for me.
Minimal-tailored with subtle street details, day-in-the-city narrative, and slightly elevated price band all feel coherent.
Unless there are strong objections, I would say we lock the capsule theme as 'Urban Drift' with that narrative and move on to T2 sketches.
We can still fine-tune small details as we see silhouettes.

No objections from me.
I will reference 'Urban Drift' and the three-moment city narrative when I start the visual identity routes in T5 and document it clearly in A3.
Having the target and price band set now will help keep the identity grounded and avoid anything that feels too luxury or too casual.

Aligned here as well.
I will keep the manufacturing notes in sync with this direction so that when we get to T3 and T8 we are not surprised by construction or cost.
For now, I will just add a short section in T1 summarizing the constraints we discussed: existing fabrics, minimal-tailored base, subtle tech details.

threads.thread_goal: Review and refine garment sketches, silhouettes, and hero looks.

messages.text:
Starting the sketches review for the 'Urban Drift' capsule.
I uploaded 12 rough silhouettes under T2: a mix of light outerwear, shirts, pants, and one dress.
They follow the minimal-tailored base with subtle street details we aligned in TH1.
Could you all take a look and comment on which ones feel strongest for the narrative and which could become hero looks for 3D in T4 and A5?

I went through the 12 options.
Quick notes:
- Look 01: cropped utility jacket with clean lines – strong candidate for a hero outer layer.
- Look 03: tapered trouser with subtle paneling – good everyday base.
- Look 05: shirt with hidden placket and contrast inner collar – fits the narrative well.
- Look 08: dress with asymmetric hem – interesting, but might push production a bit.
From a capsule balance view, I would suggest we aim for 2 outer layers, 3 tops, 3 bottoms, and maybe 1 dress or jumpsuit.
That keeps us within the 8–10 SKUs constraint and still covers the day-in-the-city story.

From a construction and sizing angle, Looks 01, 03, 05, 06, 09, and 10 seem the most straightforward to translate into T3 specs without adding too many pattern pieces.
Look 08 with the asymmetric hem and Look 12 with the layered hood might require more fitting rounds in T10 and more time in T4.
If we want to keep 3D workload manageable, I would be careful about picking too many complex shapes as hero looks.

Looking at the silhouettes with a marketing lens, Looks 01, 05, 08, and 10 read very clearly even at small sizes, which will help in e-commerce thumbnails and social teasers later in A6 and A7.
For hero looks in A5, I would lean toward:
- One strong outer layer (01 or 10)
- One clean shirt (05)
- One bottom with interesting lines (03)
- One wildcard piece (maybe 08 if production is comfortable)
That would give us variety in the 3D renders for A5 and the Internal Capsule Overview Deck A8.

I like Look 08 visually, but I am not sure how it will behave in motion.
Would it be better to test that in 3D first in T4 before we commit it as a hero look, or is that too much work?
Also, for the pants, between Looks 03 and 07, which one is easier to produce?
I am asking so we do not overload the spec pack later in T8.

Good question.
If we choose Look 08 as a hero, we will need to invest more time in T4 to get the drape right in 3D, but that might actually save us a physical sample iteration.
Between pants 03 and 07, 03 is simpler to grade and aligns better with our standard sizing systems.
I would recommend we keep 03 and drop 07 from the shortlist.

Based on all your feedback, here is a proposed shortlist of 9 SKUs from T2:
1) Look 01 – cropped utility jacket
2) Look 02 – longer overcoat (we can simplify details)
3) Look 03 – tapered trouser
4) Look 05 – hidden placket shirt
5) Look 06 – relaxed tee with subtle panel
6) Look 08 – asymmetric dress (we can refine hem)
7) Look 09 – straight trouser with clean front
8) Look 10 – short jacket with stand collar
9) Look 11 – knit top
We would drop 04, 07, and 12.
Does this feel balanced enough for the capsule and manageable for T3 and T11?

The 9-SKU list looks solid to me and stays within our 8–10 target.
We have:
- 3 outer layers (01, 02, 10)
- 3 tops (05, 06, 11)
- 2 trousers (03, 09)
- 1 dress (08)
That covers the day-in-the-city narrative.
Unless anyone sees a big gap, I would confirm these as the SKUs to move into T3 detailed specs.

From a storytelling and asset perspective, this mix works well.
For hero looks in 3D and A5, I would propose:
- Look 01 – main outerwear hero
- Look 03 – core bottom
- Look 05 – smart top
- Look 08 – statement piece
That gives us variety in silhouette and use cases for e-commerce layouts and social teasers later in T7 and T9.

I like that hero set.
Having the dress as a hero will also give us interesting motion options for teaser animations.
Just to confirm, we are not making Look 10 a hero, even though it is strong, right?
I want to be sure when I start thinking about which angles we will need for A5.

I am comfortable with 01, 03, 05, and 08 as hero looks.
They cover different pattern types and will give us a good spread for fit checks in T10.
We can still keep Look 10 as a strong supporting piece without the extra 3D workload.
If everyone agrees, we can lock these four as the hero set for T4.

Great, then we have:
- 9 SKUs confirmed from T2 for T3 specs
- Hero looks for T4: 01, 03, 05, 08
I will start cleaning up the sketches and move into flat technical drawings for these, prioritizing the hero looks first so we can feed A5.
I will also tag each look clearly in the files so it is easy to map to A2 later when we build the SKU and Colorway Matrix.

threads.thread_goal: Align on visual identity, logo lockups, and graphic direction.

messages.text:
Opening the visual identity thread for 'Urban Drift'.
I uploaded 3 routes under T5 and documented them in A3:
Route A – 'Soft Grid': calm neutrals, subtle grid lines, condensed sans serif.
Route B – 'Signal Lines': bolder accent color, diagonal lines, slightly more expressive type.
Route C – 'Quiet Tech': very minimal, almost monochrome, micro details.
All three stay within our main brand guidelines but push in different directions.
Please share which route feels most aligned with the capsule story and our target from T1.

I went through A3.
Route A feels closest to the silhouettes we have: structured but not aggressive.
Route B is exciting, but I worry the diagonals might fight with some of the panel lines on the garments, especially Looks 01 and 03.
Route C is beautiful, but maybe too quiet for the slightly elevated price band we defined in T1.
My vote is Route A, with maybe a tiny bit of Route B energy in the accent color.

Agree with 203.
Route A supports the minimal-tailored direction and lets the garments stay in focus.
I like the idea of borrowing the accent from Route B, as long as it matches one of the fabric colorways we will confirm in A2 and T11.
Route C might be better for a future capsule that is more formal.
So I would lean strongly toward Route A as the base.

From a production and packaging angle, Route A is also the most practical.
The grid and condensed type will translate well to labels and packaging graphics later in T6 without requiring special print techniques.
Route B might push us into more complex print placements.
I would support Route A with a controlled accent that we know we can reproduce consistently across materials.

I am drawn to Route B visually, but I see the point about it competing with garment lines.
If we go with Route A, could we still use some of the diagonal elements from Route B in motion assets only, like in T9, so they do not interfere with the garments themselves?
For the logo lockup, I like the stacked version in Route A best.

Yes, we can absolutely keep some of Route B's diagonals for motion-only use in T9 while keeping Route A as the core identity.
Based on the feedback so far, I will treat Route A as the main direction and fold in:
- Accent color from Route B (to be matched with fabric choices in A2 and T11)
- Diagonal motion elements for social.
If no one objects, I will mark Route A as the selected direction in A3 and T5.

Sounds good to me.
On the logo lockup, I prefer the stacked version you mentioned, especially for labels and small placements.
For the core palette, I would suggest:
- Base neutrals: off-black, warm grey
- Accent: the muted teal from Route B
- Secondary digital accent: the pale sand tone
That should sit well on the garments we are planning in T11.

Those colors are all feasible with our current suppliers.
We already have close matches for the off-black and warm grey, and the muted teal is available in at least two base fabrics.
I will note these as preferred options in A2 so we can align garments and graphics.
For labels in T6, the stacked lockup will be easier to keep legible at small sizes.

Just to be sure, are we locking the stacked logo lockup as the default for all capsule materials, or only for small formats like labels and social avatars?
I want to avoid mixing too many versions when we get to T7 and T12.

Good point.
I propose:
- Stacked lockup as the primary for the capsule (labels, packaging, social avatars, e-commerce badges)
- Horizontal lockup as a secondary option only when space is very tight.
I will document this clearly in A3.
If everyone is aligned, we can consider the stacked lockup and the palette 203 suggested as approved.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize production specs, colorways, and fabric choices.

messages.text:
Starting the specs and colorways alignment.
I uploaded a draft spec pack for the 9 SKUs under T3 and T8, and a first pass of the SKU and Colorway Matrix in A2.
For each style, I proposed 2–3 colorways using the palette we aligned in A3 and fabrics from our existing supplier list.
Please review:
- Any construction details that look risky for production
- Any color/fabric combos that feel off for the 'Urban Drift' story
We need to converge so we can sign off on T11 soon.

I went through the spec pack and A2.
Overall, the construction looks manageable.
A few notes:
- Look 01: the double topstitch on all seams might slow down production; we could limit it to key seams.
- Look 08: the asymmetric hem is fine, but we should standardize the length difference across sizes in T10.
On fabrics, I would swap the heavier twill on Look 03 for the lighter stretch twill we already use; it will improve comfort without changing the look.
No red flags on supplier availability so far.

Thanks for the review.
I can adjust Look 01 to have double topstitch only on shoulder and side seams, and keep single on the rest.
For Look 03, I am fine switching to the lighter stretch twill as long as we keep the same visual weight; I will update T3 and A2 accordingly.
Colorwise, I am wondering if we should drop the pale sand option on Look 11; it might feel too soft compared to the rest of the capsule.

From a visual identity standpoint, the pale sand on Look 11 could work as a highlight if we keep it limited.
However, if it starts to dilute the overall mood, I would rather keep sand as a background or layering color in e-commerce layouts in A6 instead of a main garment color.
I would support dropping sand for Look 11 and keeping it for graphics only.

I checked A2 and the spec previews.
For packaging graphics in T6, it will help if we keep the number of main garment colors tight.
If we drop sand from Look 11, that would simplify the palette we need to represent on labels and boxes.
Also, for Look 08, do we have a backup fabric option in case the preferred one runs low?

Yes, for Look 08 I listed a backup fabric in A2: a slightly heavier crepe from the same supplier.
It keeps the drape similar enough.
Given the feedback, I will remove the sand colorway from Look 11 and keep it as a digital-only accent.
That leaves us with off-black, warm grey, and muted teal as the main garment colors across SKUs.

With that change, the matrix in A2 looks balanced and production-friendly.
We have at least one core color in each SKU and a controlled use of teal.
From my side, I am ready to validate these color and fabric combinations for T11.
If there are no objections, we can mark the color/fabric matrix as final.

Agreed.
I will lock these choices into the individual tech packs in T3 and run a quick pass against the Production-Ready Spec Pack Checklist in A4.
Once that is done, we should be close to sign-off on T8.
If anyone spots missing trims or measurement details, please flag them now.

I noticed one small thing: in the spec for Look 02, the zipper pull is not specified.
Do we want a custom pull with the capsule lockup, or are we using a standard one?
This might affect packaging visuals and close-up shots later.

Good catch.
I would recommend a subtle custom pull with the stacked capsule lockup, but nothing too complex.
That way we can feature it in close-up shots in A6 and in the Internal Capsule Overview Deck A8 without adding much cost.
If production is ok with that, we can add it to the trims section in T3 and T8.

A simple custom pull is fine.
We already have a supplier that can do this with minimal tooling.
I will add a note in A4 to ensure the trim spec is included for Look 02 and cross-check it before final sign-off.
With that, I think we are ready to approve the spec pack once 203 finishes the checklist pass.

I have now updated all tech packs in T3 with the final colorways, fabrics, and the custom zipper pull for Look 02, and checked them against A4.
No missing measurements or trims from what I can see.
From my side, the spec pack in T8 is ready for production sign-off.

threads.thread_goal: Align on e-commerce and social launch assets and timelines.

messages.text:
Kicking off the e-commerce and social assets thread.
I uploaded draft e-commerce layouts and image guidelines under T7 and A6, plus initial social teaser concepts in T9 and A7.
Key points:
- E-comm: clean product pages with one main hero image, one detail, and one on-body shot per SKU.
- Style: neutral backgrounds with subtle grid overlays from A3.
- Social: three-part teaser sequence following the day-in-the-city narrative, using 3D hero looks from A5.
Please review and let me know if the image style and posting sequence feel right for the capsule.

The layouts in A6 look good to me.
The neutral backgrounds and subtle grid keep the focus on the garments.
For the on-body shots, can we make sure we show at least one angle that highlights the construction details, like the panel lines on Look 03 and the hem on Look 08?
That will help connect back to the work we did in T3 and T10.

Agree with 203.
Also, for the hero images, I would like to reuse some of the 3D angles from A5 where possible, especially for pre-launch.
That will save us time on photography and keep the look consistent.
For the social sequence in A7, the three-part narrative feels right; we just need to be sure the garments shown match the final colorways in A2.

I like the grid overlays and the calm tone.
One question: for mobile, are we using the same crop ratios as desktop, or do we need separate versions?
I want to avoid text or key details getting cut off in the feed.
Also, for the teaser sequence, do we plan to mix stills and motion, or keep it all static for now?

Good questions.
For e-comm, we will design with a safe area so the same images work on desktop and mobile; I documented the crop guidelines in A6.
For social, I propose:
- Teaser 1: static grid-based collage
- Teaser 2: short motion piece using 3D turntables from A5
- Teaser 3: static lookbook-style carousel
That mix should give us enough movement without overloading production.
If that sounds reasonable, I will finalize the templates in T7 and T9.

From a timing perspective, that mix is manageable.
We already have the 3D hero looks in A5, so creating the short motion piece should not add too much work.
Just make sure any close-ups do not misrepresent fabric texture or color compared to what is in A2.
I would also suggest we lock the posting sequence soon so marketing can plan the calendar in A7.

The sequence works for me.
For the e-comm product image guidelines in T7, could we add a note to always include at least one shot that shows how the garment moves, especially for Look 08 and the outerwear?
Even if it is a still, a walking pose or slight motion blur could help communicate comfort.

I can help with some of those motion-feel stills, using my photography and compositing tools.
I will just need clear notes from A6 on what is allowed so we stay consistent.
Also, for the Internal Capsule Overview Deck in A8, are we reusing the same layouts as e-comm, or do we need a slightly different structure?

For A8, I suggest a slightly different structure: more narrative, less grid, but still using the same palette and typography from A3.
We can reuse many of the e-comm images, just arranged to tell the story across the three city moments.
I will add a section in T12 describing how A8 should differ from the product pages.
On the motion-feel stills, I will update A6 with a few examples and constraints.

Before we lock the e-comm style, one last check: are we comfortable with the amount of grid overlay on the product images?
I want to be sure it does not obscure seam details or mislead about fit.
If we keep it subtle and mostly in the background, I am fine approving this style for T7.

I will keep the grid very light and mostly in negative space, away from key seams and edges.
I added overlays examples in A6 to show the safe zones.
Given the feedback, I propose we confirm this e-comm image style and the layout templates in T7 as final for this capsule.

Works for me.
On the social side, can we also confirm the posting sequence you outlined earlier so we can share it with marketing?
If we lock the three-part teaser now, they can start planning paid support and timing around the drop.

Yes, summarizing the social teaser plan in A7 and T9:
- Teaser 1: static grid collage introducing the capsule name and logo lockup.
- Teaser 2: short motion clip using 3D hero looks from A5, focusing on movement.
- Teaser 3: static carousel showing full looks in final colorways from A2.
We will schedule them in the week leading up to launch, one every two days.
If everyone is aligned, we can treat this sequence as locked.

Aligned.
This sequence reflects the capsule story well and uses the hero looks we invested in.
I will make sure any last-minute fit tweaks in T10 do not affect the visuals we already prepared.
Looking forward to seeing the final A8 deck with all of this tied together.
